mode: wrote scripts/crc8-search.py: brute-force every (byte-region x poly x init x refin x refout x xorout) CRC-8 combination, and simple XOR/sum checksums, against the 508 real frames from T009, filtered to the well-typed Call/Ack/Value/Data/Set frames (375, after excluding firmware-blob noise and frames mis-split by an internal 0xfd/0xfe byte collision)
hypothesis: can the CRC-8 algorithm that T004/T006 established was never published anywhere be recovered now that real (message, crc) pairs exist, instead of guessing blind
verdict: CONFIRMED, the CRC-8 mystery is solved: poly=0x07 (the plain/standard CRC-8 polynomial), init=0x00, no bit reflection, computed over [type,id,src,dst,cmd,payload...] (frame[1:-2], i.e. everything between the 0xfd SOF and the CRC byte), then the result is XORed with a constant 0xFD to get the final CRC byte. Matches 368/375 (98%) of the filtered real frames exactly. The 7 exceptions are all short/irregular sub-frames (e.g. Acks with a 5-byte body instead of the usual 9, one 17-byte Data frame, one 18-byte frame that may itself be leftover noise) - not yet explained, but too small and too structurally different to doubt the core algorithm. crc8-search.py kept in scripts/ for rerunning against future captures (e.g. to explain the 7 stragglers, or once a real 'Connect' capture exists).

mode: 3 parallel research agents: (1) mine ../reverb-g2 for reusable ideas, (2) Wine/Proton compatibility for legacy Axis Neuron, (3) live-streaming Axis Neuron's motion data into Unity/a game engine
hypothesis: does the sibling project have transferable methodology we haven't used yet, is Wine a viable way to run Axis Neuron long-term instead of a real Windows box, and is there a documented way to get live mocap data into Unity without waiting on the full protocol reverse-engineering effort
verdict: three distinct answers. (1) reverb-g2: no direct Wine/game-engine/licensing precedent (different problem shape - HP's driver isn't dongle-gated), but its whole thesis validates this project's Path A priority: reverse-engineer once, then run natively, don't keep depending on a vendor Windows app long-term. (2) Wine: zero WinehQ AppDB entries or community reports for Axis Neuron either way; the CP210x/tty passthrough mechanism itself is well-documented and should work in principle, but one real risk surfaced (a Wine bug capping reported serial baud rate at 115200, which could silently break high-rate IMU streaming) - untested, not to be relied on without trying it empirically first. (3) Unity: real, documented, license-free path exists and doesn't require any of the protocol reverse-engineering - legacy Axis Neuron has built-in BVH Broadcasting (Settings > Broadcasting, TCP/UDP ports 7001 raw BVH / 7003 calculated data, with an 'Axis Legacy' skeleton-type option matching this exact PN32/PNHU01 hardware generation), consumable in Unity via the open-source keijiro/NeuronAnimator plugin or Noitom's own official Unity SDK package - both just connect to that broadcast, no Axis Studio and no license needed. A community VRPN fork (vrpn-PerceptionNeuron, explaining the vrpnNoitom.dll seen in docs/04's static analysis) exists but talks to the hub directly via hidapi, bypassing Axis Neuron entirely - same reverse-engineering problem as this project, not a shortcut, not worth pursuing separately.

verdict: CONFIRMED on both counts. New protocol surface: (1) GetConfig key=0x01 HubFirmwareVersion and key=0x15 HubSerialNumber, both already in KEYS from pelrun's table but not previously seen in a real capture, now confirmed (key=0x15 payload decodes as ASCII, hub serial-ish string). (2) A Call addressed dst=00 (payload 03 00 02 00 00) - first time seen targeting neither the hub (0xc0) nor a sensor's usual node id. (3) Function payload 03 0b 00 00 00 - new, not in docs/01's known-commands list, triggers a Value ack plus a type=Data frame keyed 0x7a (also undocumented). (4) Function payload 02 01 00 00 00 (repeated 3x) - new, Value-only response, no Data frame. (5) Two Calls addressed dst=a1 - the single sensor's own node id, not the hub - first time a Call has targeted a sensor directly instead of going through 0xc0; payloads 04 02 00 00 00 and 00 00 00 00 00. (6) One type=Set (0x0a) frame, key=0x0f, 51-byte payload of dense packed-looking binary (plausibly float32 calibration coefficients) - the first Set-type frame captured in this project at all, timing-correlated with the photographed rotate+sphere-collection calibration step. None of these are decoded field-by-field yet, just newly confirmed to exist and roughly where they sit in the sequence (Connect -> Disconnect -> re-GetConfig -> node-enum triggers -> the dst=00/dst=a1/Set cluster above -> IMU resumes). Sensor health check: the single sensor (hub node id 0xa1, confirmed consistent byte-for-byte across all 2260/2261 real IMUdata frames in the pcapng, one stray byte discarded as noise) streamed cleanly through the whole calibration session and, checked live afterward with the new scripts/pn-meter.py while physically unmoved, streams steadily at ~60 fps with no drops or node-id changes - the calibration/demagnetize procedure did not break the sensor or its pairing.
